headline: Approved $211,000 sale of 81 Church Avenue and a lease for the BEALS Senior Community Center; tabled Parcel 16-3 Perkins Street.
summary: Members approved a lease with the Bristol Burlington Health District, the sale of 81 Church Avenue for $211,000, and the sale of 93 Tuttle Road for $1,500. They tabled Parcel 16-3 Perkins Street and Lots 6, 7 & 8 Witches Rock Road, and sent 30 Cross Street to the City Council for approval as a training facility.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the September 8, 2026 Regular Meeting, all in favor.
Approved accepting the donation of Parcel 19-10 Perkins Street from the Clinton Roberts Foundation, subject to an appraisal; all in favor.
Tabled Parcel 16-3 Perkins Street; all in favor.
Approved initiating a quitclaim of 99 Main Street for no consideration; all in favor.
Referred 30 Cross Street to the City Council for approval as a joint Police and Fire training facility; all in favor.
Approved the lease with the Bristol Burlington Health District for the BEALS Senior Community Center at the same rate, beginning January 1, 2027; all in favor.
Approved accepting Brian Whitford's offer of $211,000 for 81 Church Avenue; all in favor.
Tabled Lots 6, 7 & 8 Witches Rock Road until next month and asked all parties to appear; all in favor.
Approved the sale of 93 Tuttle Road for $1,500; all in favor. The matter goes to the City Council.
Placed Lot 4 & Lot 6 (aka 164) Union Street on next month's agenda.
Explained that the request for Lot 2-2 North Pond Street is not possible at this time, because a driveway cannot go through City open space.

plain_text:
Page 1 
 
 
City of Bristol 
BRISTOL, CONNECTICUT  06010 
 
REAL ESTATE COMMITTEE 
MINUTES 
MEETING OF TUESDAY OCTOBER 5, 2026 
5:30 P.M. 
CALL TO ORDER: 
By: Chairman Hahn Time: 5:30 p.m. Place: City Hall 
111 North Main Street 
Meeting Room 1-1 
 
NAME PRESENT ABSENT 
Councilman Greg Hahn, Chairperson X  
Councilman Erick Rosengren X  
Councilman Mark Dickau X  
 
1.    Administrative Matters 
 
a.    Approval of Minutes - September 8, 2026 Regular Meeting 
MOTION:    To approve the minutes of the Regular Meeting of September 8, 2026. 
BY:    Councilman Dickau          Seconded: Councilman Rosengren 
For:    All in favor 
2.    Public Participation 
Joanne Caron, 425 Burlington Avenue, Bristol, appeared before the Committee to discuss 
the proposed subdivision of her property and the possibility of obtaining an easement across 
a city-owned parcel.  
3.    New Business 
The Committee voted to take several Old Business items out of order. The substantive 
discussion and action on those items are recorded under Item 4, Old Business, below. 
 
MOTION:    To take Item 4(d)(ii), 93 Tuttle Road, out of order. 
BY:    Councilman Dickau          Seconded: Councilman Rosengren 
For:    All in favor 
 
MOTION:    To take Item 4(f), Lot 2-2 North Pond Street, out of order. 
BY:    Councilman Dickau          Seconded: Councilman Rosengren 
For:    All in favor 
 
MOTION:    To take Item 4(c), Lots 6, 7 & 8 Witches Rock Road, out of order.
Page 2 
BY:    Councilman Dickau          Seconded: Councilman Rosengren 
For:    All in favor 
 
MOTION:    To take Item 4(b), 81 Church Avenue, out of order. 
 
BY:    Councilman Dickau          Seconded: Councilman Rosengren 
For:    All in favor 
 
a.    Parcel 19-10 Perkins Street - 7.5 acres Attorney Ziogas appeared for this portion of the 
meeting. The matter returned with a positive recommendation from the 8-24 review. 
MOTION:    To accept the donation of Parcel 19-10 Perkins Street from the Clinton Roberts 
Foundation, subject to an appraisal. 
 
BY:    Councilman Dickau          Seconded: Councilman Rosengren 
For:    All in favor 
 
b.    Parcel 16-3 Perkins Street - 3 acres The proposed donation is contingent upon the 
City waiving its right of first refusal. Planning recommended that the City not waive its right of 
first refusal. 
MOTION:    To table Item 3(b), Parcel 16-3 Perkins Street. 
BY:    Councilman Rosengren          Seconded: Councilman Dickau 
For:    All in favor 
 
c.    99 Main Street 
 
MOTION:    To initiate a quitclaim of the subject piece of property for no consideration. 
BY:    Councilman Dickau          Seconded: Councilman Rosengren 
For:    All in favor 
 
d.    30 Cross Street 
 
MOTION:    To return 30 Cross Street to the City Council for approval for use as a joint 
Police and Fire training facility. 
 
BY:    Councilman Dickau          Seconded: Councilman Rosengren 
For:    All in favor 
 
e.    Map 65, Lot 9, Marsh Road The Committee discussed City-owned property on Marsh 
Road. 
 
MOTION:    To add Map 65, Lot 7, Marsh Road, City of Bristol, to this item. 
BY:    Councilman Dickau          Seconded: Councilman Rosengren 
For:    All in favor 
 
No further action was needed. 
4.    Old Business 
a.    Lease with the Bristol Burlington Health District (BBHD) - BEALS Senior 
Community Center The lease covers 7,001 sq. ft. at $17.40 per sq. ft. The new lease would
Page 3 
begin January 1, 2027. 
 
MOTION:    To approve the lease as written at the same rate. 
BY:    Councilman Dickau          Seconded: Councilman Rosengren 
For:    All in favor 
 
b.    81 Church Avenue (Fire Company No. 3) This item was taken out of order. One offer 
was received from Brian Whitford. 
MOTION:    To accept Brian Whitford's offer of $211,000 for 81 Church Avenue. 
 
BY:    Councilman Dickau          Seconded: Councilman Rosengren 
For:    All in favor 
 
c.    Lots 6, 7 & 8 Witches Rock Road This item was taken out of order and was the third 
Old Business item heard. Nancy Haynes appeared to discuss the RFP results. Three bids 
were received: $25,088 from Derrick Ruegg, proposing to leave the property as is; $7,500 
from Tyler Stevens, who did not specify the intended use of the lot; and $6,000 from Brett 
Benincasa, an adjoining property owner. The Committee had additional questions regarding 
the latter two offers. 
 
MOTION:    To table Lots 6, 7 & 8 Witches Rock Road until next month and request that all parties 
appear. 
 
BY:    Councilman Rosengren          Seconded: Councilman Dickau 
For:    All in favor 
 
d.    List of possible encroaching property owners on City-owned properties 
i.    64 Kilmartin - Ryan Heller is in the process of, or may have completed, running the 
property line to determine the extent of any encroachment. Attorney Steeg will follow up 
on the status. 
ii.    93 Tuttle Road - This item was taken out of order. Chairman Hahn reviewed responses 
to correspondence regarding the property. 
 
MOTION:    To approve the sale of the small City-owned property at 93 Tuttle Road for 
$1,500. 
 
BY:    Councilman Rosengren          Seconded: Councilman Dickau 
For:    All in favor 
 
Mrs. Cockayne stated that she believed $500.00 was a fair price because the land is 
unusable. She stated that the swing set has been removed. The matter will proceed to 
the City Council, and Attorney Steeg will send Mrs. Cockayne a letter. 
 
e.    Lot 4 & Lot 6 (aka 164) Union Street The matter will be placed on next month's 
agenda. If the interested party does not appear, the Committee indicated that it will not 
place the matter back on a future agenda. 
 
f.    Lot 2-2 North Pond Street This item was taken out of order and was heard second. Ms. 
Caron and her husband appeared for this portion of the meeting. Attorney Steeg shared 
a map with the Carons and explained that their request is not possible at this time 
because a driveway cannot go through City open space.
Page 4 
g.    135 East Main Street - Status The closing was expected to occur Thursday. The city is  
awaiting a check from an attorney in New York. 
 
5.    Adjournment 
 
MOTION:    To adjourn the meeting at 6:14 p.m. 
 
BY:    Councilman Rosengren          Seconded: Councilman Dickau 
For:    All in favor
